book_title: Chapter 8: Stage 2 VCP Squeeze, Multi-Timeframe Tape & Upward Stop Ratchet
question: Does the November 20 tape keep the existing Stage 2 holding intact, and how does an upward-only stop ratchet protect profits inside a Downtrend regime?

epigraph.quote: Trim half into a Stage 2 valuation rally to rebuild Downtrend cash, and ratchet the remaining stop right beneath the rising 50-day average.
epigraph.author: Technical & Risk-Management Desk, November 20, 2026

web_blocks.html: The US equity market remains entrenched in a Downtrend as of November 20, 2026. Only 38.8% of S&P 500 stocks hold above their 50-day moving averages (46.9% above 200-day), while 10 distribution days have hit over the past 25 sessions. Just 1 of 11 sectors holds above its 20-day average, and US 10-year Treasury yields sit at 5.04% (2-year at 4.76%). Against that weak backdrop, AvePoint (NASDAQ: AVPT) holds a clean Weinstein Stage 2 (Markup) trend in both facts (Stage 2) and snapshots (STAGE_2, BUY_AT_CMP_NO_FOMO, CLEAR_FOR_CONSIDERATION). At $16.49 (-2.66% 1D, -0.36% 1W, +2.55% 1M, +24.55% 3M, +60.25% 6M, +30.98% 1Y), AVPT trades +6.39% above its rising 10-week EMA ($15.50; facts ema10w_approx $15.43) and +8.63% above its rising 50-day SMA ($15.18).

Trimming 50% (76.6 sh) immediately into Cash and ratcheting the hard stop up to $15.05 lifts remaining-stake R:R to 1.92:1 while cutting max loss to -$110.35 (0.15% of net worth).

web_blocks.html: 1W / 1D / 4H Alignment & VCP Contraction: Across all three timeframes, AvePoint shows constructive supply absorption rather than distribution. On the weekly chart, 1W RSI(14) is 66.79 and 63-day relative strength leads SPY by +34.19% (+24.83% over 28 days) [2]. On the daily chart, 1D RSI(14) sits at 54.00 while Bollinger bandwidth tightened further from 10.32% to 8.37% with a $0.65 ATR(14). Friday's -2.66% pullback to $16.49 ran on 3.16 million shares—0.91x the 30-day average and 0.77x the 20-day average, with a 63-day volume dry-up ratio of 0.31. On the 4-hour chart, 4H RSI sits at 50.41 just below the 4H 20-EMA ($16.51) and atop the 4H 50-SMA ($16.45), with intraday_4h_turn: false. Both facts (Stage 2) and snapshots (STAGE_2) classify the trend identically, differing only by seven cents on weekly EMA rounding ($15.50 vs. $15.43).

Upward-Only Stop Ratchet & 50% De-Risking Math ($12.68 → $15.05): On November 17, our 153.2332-share Schwab stake carried a structural stop at $12.68. With the position barely in profit (+$26.82 / +1.07% at $16.315 cost), US portfolio cash at just 3.38% ($2,540.35 vs. 22.0% Downtrend floor across 10 distribution days), and Finviz 5Y beta at 1.07 (confirming no defensive exemption alongside the 0.69 1Y trailing beta), holding 100% at a 1.39:1 R:R ($14.50) conflicts with portfolio risk discipline. We therefore execute TRIM_INTO_STRENGTH: sell 76.6 shares (~50%, ~$1,263.13 proceeds) into USD Cash immediately—lifting cash toward 5.06% (~$3,803.48) and halving weight from 3.36% to 1.68%—and trail the remaining 76.6332 shares ($1,263.69 MV) behind an upward-ratcheted hard stop at $15.05. That stop sits $0.13 (0.20x ATR14) below the rising 50-day SMA ($15.18) and $0.22 above Pivot S1 ($14.83), tightening protection by +$2.37 per share (+18.7%) vs. $12.68. Downside drops to -8.7% (-$1.44/sh = -$110.35 max loss, just 0.15% of net worth) vs. +16.7% (+$2.76/sh) to $19.25—restoring a clean 1.92:1 remaining-stake R:R (≥1.50:1 hurdle).

Options Overlay & Short-Float Dynamics: Our live options screen marks AVPT as NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID because bid-ask spreads exceed 14% or lack open interest. Accordingly, options strategies are excluded; equity-only execution governs the position. Short interest stands at 11.50 million shares (8.22% of float, 4.28 days to cover), while institutional ownership rose +2.93% to 58.90% alongside S&P SmallCap 600 index demand. On our remaining 76.6332 shares, a decisive daily close above the $17.52 52-week high on >4.5M volume opens a run toward Pivot R1 ($18.44) and our $19.25 Base Case trim zone (sell 38.3 shares).

web_blocks.title: TAPE DISCIPLINE IN A 10-DISTRIBUTION-DAY DOWNTREND
paragraphs: A Downtrend tape with 38.8% S&P 500 breadth, 10 distribution days, and 3.38% US portfolio cash demands proactive liquidity—not passive hope. Selling 76.6 shares (~$1,263.13) now and ratcheting our hard stop from $12.68 up to $15.05 (just below the rising $15.18 50-day SMA) restores 1.92:1 remaining-stake R:R and caps residual risk at 0.15% of net worth before any Stage 4 slide.

book_paragraphs: Turning from valuation to the November 20, 2026 tape explains why our decisions for new money and existing shares diverge. First, look at the macro weather. The S&P 500 sits in a confirmed Downtrend with only 38.8 percent of stocks above their 50-day moving averages and 10 distribution days logged over the past 25 sessions. Only one of eleven market sectors holds above its 20-day average, while 10-year Treasury yields remain elevated at 5.04 percent.

Inside that hostile market, AvePoint remains a stubborn Weinstein Stage 2 leader. Both our quantitative facts ledger and TradingView snapshot classify AVPT in Stage 2 Markup, with zero stage divergence—only a minor seven-cent rounding difference on the 10-week EMA between 15.50 dollars in snapshots and 15.43 dollars in facts. At 16.49 dollars, shares have gained 24.6 percent over three months and 60.3 percent over six months, sitting just 5.88 percent below their 17.52 dollar 52-week high.

All four major trendlines slope upward beneath price. The 10-week EMA sits at 15.50 dollars (+6.39 percent extension), the 50-day SMA sits at 15.18 dollars (+8.63 percent extension), the 30-week SMA sits at 13.01 dollars (+26.75 percent), and the 200-day SMA sits at 12.22 dollars (+34.94 percent). Notice how fast support has risen: the 50-day SMA climbed from 13.80 dollars twenty-one sessions ago to 15.18 dollars today.

Multi-timeframe oscillators show calm consolidation rather than blow-off exhaustion. Weekly RSI stands at 66.79, backed by 34.2 percent 63-day relative outperformance against the S&P 500. Daily RSI sits at 54.00 as Bollinger bandwidth compressed from 10.32 percent down to 8.37 percent—a tight Volatility Contraction Pattern with a 65-cent Average True Range. On the 4-hour chart, RSI reads 50.41 just under the 4-hour 20-EMA at 16.51 dollars, with no intraday reversal trigger yet.

Volume confirms institutional patience. Friday's 2.66 percent dip to 16.49 dollars traded 3.16 million shares, or 0.91 times the 30-day average and 0.77 times the 20-day average. Meanwhile, 11.50 million shares remain sold short (8.22 percent of the float, 4.28 days to cover), and institutional ownership ticked up 2.93 percent to 58.90 percent. Because options spreads exceed 14 percent with thin open interest, AVPT is strictly an equity-only vehicle.

That Stage 2 structure paired with a ten-distribution-day Downtrend drives a two-part defensive move. Holding 100 percent of our shares at just 3.38 percent portfolio cash and a 1.07 five-year Finviz beta would leave too much capital exposed on a thin 1.07 percent gain. Instead, we sell 76.6 shares immediately into cash (~1,263.13 dollars) and ratchet the hard stop on our remaining 76.6332 shares up from 12.68 dollars to 15.05 dollars—thirteen cents below the rising 50-day SMA at 15.18 dollars and above Pivot S1 at 14.83 dollars.

book_subsections.title: Why Trimming 50% and Ratcheting to $15.05 Beats Holding 100%
paragraphs: One of the hardest habits in portfolio management is sizing down a Stage 2 winner before support snaps. Because our Schwab shares were bought at 16.315 dollars and sit just 1.07 percent in profit, holding 153.2332 shares behind a 14.50 dollar stop offered only 1.39-to-1 reward-to-risk and risked 304.93 dollars while US portfolio cash sat at 3.38 percent against a 22.0 percent Downtrend floor.

Selling 76.6 shares today immediately puts 1,263.13 dollars into Treasury cash and halves our position weight from 3.36 percent to 1.68 percent. Ratcheting the hard stop on the remaining 76.6332 shares up to 15.05 dollars cuts residual downside to minus 8.7 percent (110.35 dollars, or 0.15 percent of net worth) against 16.7 percent upside to 19.25 dollars—lifting remaining reward-to-risk to a disciplined 1.92-to-1.

book_subsections.title: Reading the 1W, 1D, and 4H Timeframes Together
paragraphs: Looking across three chart intervals prevents both premature selling and reckless chasing. On the weekly chart, AVPT remains clearly constructive: price holds 6.39 percent above the 10-week EMA and Weekly RSI sits at 66.79. There is zero weekly distribution pattern on the chart, and the 30-week average at 13.01 dollars rises steadily beneath the base.

On the daily chart, Bollinger bandwidth squeezed from 10.32 percent down to 8.37 percent inside a tight shelf between 15.62 dollars (the 20-day swing low) and 17.52 dollars (the 52-week high). Zooming into the 4-hour chart explains why near-term momentum has paused: price sits just under the 4-hour 20-EMA at 16.51 dollars with 4H RSI at 50.41 and no upward turn printed. That stalemate resolves either on a high-volume breakout above 17.52 dollars or a drop through our 15.05 dollar stop.

book_subsections.title: Why Options Are Excluded Under NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID
paragraphs: In prior sessions, we examined whether January 2027 call debit spreads could express bullish exposure with bounded capital risk. Our November 20 live options scan settles that question decisively: AVPT options carry bid-ask spreads above 14 percent or lack meaningful open interest, earning a NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID flag.

Crossing wide bid-ask spreads on illiquid small-cap options gives away double-digit edge on day one and traps you when trying to exit in a Downtrend. When option chains fail liquidity gates, institutional discipline requires trading equity only—or holding existing shares with a clean stop.

book_subsections.title: Institutional Ownership, 8.22% Short Float & Pivot Roadmap
paragraphs: Tracking ownership and key price levels maps both upside and downside triggers cleanly. Institutions now hold 58.90 percent of shares (+2.93 percent recent change) alongside 33.44 percent reported insider ownership on Finviz (22.66 percent director-and-officer beneficial ownership per the 2026 proxy). Meanwhile, 11.50 million shares remain sold short, representing 4.28 days of average volume.

Overhead, the 52-week high at 17.52 dollars is the clear ignition gate, followed by Pivot R1 at 18.44 dollars, our Base Case trim level at 19.25 dollars (sell 38.3 shares), and Pivot R2 at 19.78 dollars. Beneath price, the 20-day EMA (16.33 dollars), 10-week EMA (15.50 dollars), and rising 50-day SMA (15.18 dollars) stand directly above our 15.05 dollar ratcheted hard stop and Pivot S1 (14.83 dollars).

book_subsections.title: Reconciling 1.07 Finviz Beta vs. 0.69 Realized Beta Inside a 234% Exposure Book
paragraphs: Beta context matters at both the single-stock and portfolio levels. Across our 75,110.60 dollar US portfolio, leveraged funds, options, and high-beta hardware names push effective S&P 500 exposure to 234.2 percent, with nine correlated positions representing 40.31 percent of net worth.

Crucially, AvePoint's one-year realized trailing beta reads 0.69 in our factpack ledger, yet its five-year Finviz beta reads 1.07—typical for a mid-cap software stock trading above 58 times ex-SBC free cash flow. Because neither beta grants a defensive exemption during a ten-distribution-day Downtrend, trimming 76.6 shares immediately and trailing the remaining 76.6332 shares behind a tight 15.05 dollar stop is the disciplined choice.

book_subsections.title: Reading Volatility Contraction (8.37% BBW) & 0.77x Pullback Volume
paragraphs: Bollinger bandwidth measures how tightly daily prices are coiling relative to their 20-day standard deviation. Between November 17 and November 20, AvePoint's Bollinger bandwidth narrowed from 10.32 percent down to 8.37 percent, while 14-day Average True Range held steady at 65 cents. Meanwhile, its 63-day volume dry-up ratio sits at 0.31, showing that overhead supply has steadily thinned out as shares consolidated beneath 17.52 dollars.

Equally revealing is how the stock behaved on Friday's 2.66 percent dip to 16.49 dollars. Volume reached 3.16 million shares, or 0.91 times the 30-day average and just 0.77 times the 20-day average. Institutions were not dumping positions ahead of the weekend. That quiet tape supports keeping a trimmed 76.6332-share runner behind our 15.05 dollar stop after harvesting 76.6 shares into cash.

book_subsections.title: Navigating a 38.8% Breadth Downtrend Without Chasing
paragraphs: Market regime context explains why Stage 2 leadership alone cannot justify fresh capital when valuation is stretched. On November 20, 2026, only 38.8 percent of S&P 500 constituents traded above their 50-day moving averages, and only 46.9 percent held above their 200-day averages. Just one of eleven sectors sat above its 20-day average, while ten institutional distribution days stacked up over twenty-five trading sessions.

Historically, holding oversized software positions at 58 to 63 times owner earnings during a ten-distribution-day Downtrend leaves portfolios vulnerable to gap-downs, as Stage 4 peer DigitalOcean showed when it fell 38.8 percent below its 50-day average. Trimming 50 percent today into cash while trailing our remaining 1.68 percent stake behind a 15.05 dollar stop balances upside participation with liquidity defense.

book_subsections.title: What a Breakdown Below $15.05 vs. a Breakout Above $17.52 Confirms
paragraphs: Clear technical rules remove guesswork before either boundary triggers. On the downside, a daily or weekly close below 15.05 dollars slices through both the 10-week EMA (15.50 dollars) and the rising 50-day SMA (15.18 dollars), signaling institutional distribution and triggering an immediate exit of all remaining 76.6332 Schwab shares with downside capped at 110.35 dollars.

On the upside, a decisive close above the 17.52 dollar 52-week high on more than 4.5 million shares forces short sellers holding 11.50 million shares (8.22 percent of float) to cover into S&P SmallCap 600 inflows, carrying our retained runner toward Pivot R1 (18.44 dollars) and our 19.25 dollar Base Case trim target.

book_subsections.title: Industry Breadth & Software-Infrastructure Sector Context
paragraphs: Looking beneath the headline S&P 500 index into AvePoint's Software-Infrastructure industry explains why relative strength stands out. Within AvePoint's peer group, only 43.0 percent of stocks sit above their 200-day exponential moving averages, and just 41.0 percent hold above their 50-day exponential moving averages. Most mid-cap software charts remain trapped in sideways or downward repair phases.

AvePoint, by contrast, trades 34.94 percent above its 200-day SMA (12.22 dollars) and 8.63 percent above its rising 50-day SMA (15.18 dollars), earning a Base Building Breakout tag on normal volume. Holding existing shares honors that outperformance while valuation keeps fresh cash sidelined.

book_subsections.title: Comparing AVPT's Stage 2 Tape Against Snapshot Peers
paragraphs: Comparing live November 20 charts across our snapshot universe highlights AvePoint's rare relative strength. DigitalOcean plunged 38.8 percent below its 50-day SMA into Stage 4 with a 31.04 daily RSI, while Alphabet slid 17.69 percent below its 50-day SMA into Stage 4 with a 27.78 daily RSI. Even Microsoft rests 6.79 percent below its 50-day SMA in Stage 3 consolidation.

Only AvePoint and Klaviyo maintain Stage 2 uptrends among those technology names. Klaviyo sits extended 12.49 percent above its 10-week EMA and 18.80 percent above its 50-day SMA, whereas AvePoint coils calmly 6.39 percent above its 10-week EMA. That clean tape supports trailing our remaining 76.6332-share Schwab runner behind the 15.05 dollar stop after today's 50 percent trim.
